title: DCKV: Learned Transform Coding of the Prompt KV Cache in Hybrid Language Models
summary: The method replaces raw bf16 storage of the full-attention KV cache in hybrid language models with a learned transform codec whose quantizer and entropy models are trained end-to-end against the frozen LM. The cost is a training stage for the codec, extra encode/decode compute on every prompt reuse, and a measurable quality loss of up to 1.8 to 3.6 benchmark points depending on the compression ratio. It can fail when the target model differs from the model the codec was trained against, when workloads are dominated by short prompts where the cache is not the bottleneck, or when the entropy model's token conditioning is unavailable at decode time.
rationale: The compression claim is strong and relevant to prompt reuse, but it requires training a codec per model and is validated only on a 2B hybrid model, so it is not yet adoptable as off-the-shelf production tooling for a small team.

claims.statement: The method replaces raw bf16 storage of the full-attention KV cache in hybrid language models with a learned transform codec whose quantizer and entropy models are trained end-to-end against the frozen LM. The cost is a training stage for the codec, extra encode/decode compute on every prompt reuse, and a measurable quality loss of up to 1.8 to 3.6 benchmark points depending on the compression ratio. It can fail when the target model differs from the model the codec was trained against, when workloads are dominated by short prompts where the cache is not the bottleneck, or when the entropy model's token conditioning is unavailable at decode time.

DCKV stores a compressed prompt token in more than 55x fewer bytes than bf16 with at most 1.8 points degradation on three long-context benchmarks, and more than 100x fewer bytes at up to 3.6 points loss.
